clue.text: Cut around tough fish

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the word for cut round so it runs the other way

parts.note: to cut hair or a hedge is to clip it
tough meat or work is hard

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: slice round a fish whose flesh is tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like the definition, but it is the word that 'around' turns round; the fish is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily sea creature of the herring family, often sold tinned in tomato sauce.

clue.text: What's written at foot of page about the French philosopher

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.words: What's written at foot of page
parts.note: PTO, 'please turn over', is written at the bottom of a page
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A footnote on a page discusses a French thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: PTO stands for 'please turn over'; 'about' puts it round LA.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Socrates and author of the Republic.

clue.text: Pass over English hill-range, being one of the lake poets

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the next ones

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a ridge is a long line of hills

explanation.surface: A walker crosses an English range and turns out to be a Lakeland poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lake Poets were Wordsworth, Coleridge and Southey, who lived in England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Taylor, author of The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, lived in the Lake District with Wordsworth.

clue.text: A sailor heard making attack

indicators.note: heard tells us the words before it are spoken, and we write a different spelling

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor, so this is 'a salt'

explanation.surface: A seaman is overheard planning an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A salt' and ASSAULT are said almost the same, the stress falling on the second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent physical onslaught, as in a military charge or a crime against a person.

clue.text: Ma noticed untidy country — cleaning-up required

indicators.note: untidy suggests the letters of the words before it are in disorder

parts.note: a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Mother noticed the country was a mess and wanted it cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' rearranges MANOTICED into DECONTAMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing dangerous substances such as radiation or chemicals from an area is a thorough clean.

clue.text: Food I start to love after time of abstinence

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the time of abstinence

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of love is used

explanation.surface: Someone longing for proper food once a fast is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dried pulse, eaten in soups and dhal.

clue.text: Understatement that could be contrived by t.s Eliot

indicators.note: contrived means artfully arranged, so the poet's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A play on modest phrasing that the poet T S Eliot might have devised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges the letters TSELIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech that affirms by denying the opposite, as in 'not bad' for good.

clue.text: Brown knight going to work in a sleeveless garment

annotationWithheld.why: Brown knight going to work in a sleeveless garment (4,3): TAN + K gives TANK, but no reading of 'going to work in' gives TOP without a letter shared or invented
annotationWithheld.clue: Brown knight going to work in a sleeveless garment

clue.text: City-dwellers can be solitary types, academic admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: loners are people who keep to themselves
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A remark that urban folk can be loners, scholars included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' only links the definition to the wordplay; 'admitted' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of the British capital are urban residents.

clue.text: Points of view put by old Germans

explanation.surface: Opinions offered by ancient Germanic tribesmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put by' is only a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspectives on a question; also the Germanic tribe that settled in England and gave it its name.

clue.text: Understand what lady in summer dress might have

definitions.text: what lady in summer dress might have

explanation.surface: Grasping what a woman wears for summer.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: a light summer frock is often made of cotton, so she has it on.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp or realise something is the informal phrasal verb; a woman in a light frock has that fabric on her.

clue.text: Capsize in open vessel

parts.note: overt means done openly
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: Tipping over while sitting in an open boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a boat, but here it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn upside down, as a boat does when it tips over.

clue.text: Military entertainment — it can be shoddy stuff as well

parts.note: tat is cheap, poor-quality goods
too means also

explanation.surface: A grumble that an army show can also be cheap rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: A tattoo is an evening military display, like the Edinburgh one.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening display of marching bands and drills put on by the armed forces.

clue.text: Old us soldier without aim to join army feud

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: vet is American short for a veteran, an old soldier
an end is an aim or goal
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An aimless American veteran enlists in a feuding army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', not 'lacking', so it signals a container, not a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running blood feud between families, seeking revenge.

clue.text: Six college servants entertaining any number of noble gentlemen

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: scouts are college servants at Oxford
N is used in maths for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Six servants in a college hosting a crowd of aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts N inside SCOUTS. At Oxford a scout is a college servant who looks after students' rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers ranking below an earl and above a baron in the British nobility.

clue.text: Yielding to drink? Please cut down by 50%

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: cut down by 50% means only the first half of please survives

explanation.surface: Someone being asked to drink just half as much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down by 50%' keeps PLE, the first half of PLEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple means pliant or bending easily, giving way under pressure.

clue.text: A pint vile, disgusting? That's sad

indicators.note: disgusting is used loosely as an instruction to jumble the letters

explanation.surface: A drinker complaining about a revolting pint of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disgusting' rearranges APINTVILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mournful, as a melancholy cry or song sounds.

clue.text: Cry on the way out, being denied kiss and words of acceptance

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the first piece comes before the next

parts.note: to sob is to cry

indicators.note: being denied means the kiss is taken away from the way out

parts.note: an exit is the way out

explanation.surface: A tearful exit made without a goodbye kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being denied' removes X from EXIT, leaving EIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A resigned phrase meaning very well, let it happen.

clue.text: PM's obvious victory

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is': the Prime Minister is what follows

parts.note: a bald statement is plain and obvious
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister enjoys a clear-cut win.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Baldwin was British Prime Minister three times between the wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin, Conservative leader of Britain in the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Sound of bell — was guide thrilled?

parts.note: a ting is a light ringing sound
led means guided, as a guide did

explanation.surface: A bell rings: was the guide excited?
explanation.definitionFit: Tingled means felt a prickle of excitement.

clue.text: Home needs certain tools, emphatically

parts.note: in means at home
spades are digging tools

explanation.surface: A house needs some garden tools, and badly.
explanation.definitionFit: In large amounts or to a great degree, as in 'he has talent in abundance'.

clue.text: The yellow used in the chemistry lab?

definitions.text: The yellow used in the chemistry lab?

parts.words: The yellow used in the chemistry lab?
parts.note: suggests a paint or dye, but means the yellow element a chemist works with

explanation.surface: Which yellow colouring do chemists use?
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow' looks like a colour in a paint box; it is the pale yellow non-metal element, symbol S.
explanation.definitionFit: The element brimstone is a bright yellow solid used in many lab reactions.

clue.text: One left in Arab country may look after the wells there

definitions.text: One left in Arab country may look after the wells there

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the pair go into the country

parts.note: Oman is a country in the Arabian peninsula
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone stationed in an Arabian state to tend the wells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I and L inside OMAN. Read as a whole, the clue describes the worker too.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker in the petroleum industry, tending the drilling sites of the Gulf.

clue.text: On the whole, you get exhausted with a couple of learners in tow

indicators.note: in tow means the other pieces trail behind, following it

parts.note: all in means worn out
L is a learner driver, so two of them are LL

explanation.surface: Feeling worn out after taking two learner drivers along.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner driver's plate in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall, considering everything together.

clue.text: Burdened camel finally comes to Yemeni location

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of camel

parts.note: Aden is a port city in Yemen

explanation.surface: A loaded camel finally reaches a city in Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded or weighed down.

clue.text: What sounds like an addition to the shops in capital city

indicators.note: says the words for a shop addition are spoken and then respelt

parts.note: a new deli, a delicatessen newly opened, adds to the shops

explanation.surface: A riddle about a newly opened shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital of India is said the same as a newly opened delicatessen.
explanation.definitionFit: The seat of the Indian government.

clue.text: Greeted in hospital — wasn't feeling well

parts.note: H is the map symbol for hospital
ailed means was ill

explanation.surface: A patient in hospital being welcomed while ill.
explanation.definitionFit: To call out to or welcome someone.

clue.text: Evil, evil sailor

parts.note: sin is wickedness, evil
bad means evil

explanation.surface: A villainous seaman, wicked twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised first 'Evil' is a noun, the second an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The voyager of the Arabian Nights, who made seven voyages.

clue.text: Knight and 'ussars? They invaded Britain

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
hussars are cavalry horsemen; the apostrophe drops the H as a cockney would, so drop it from horsemen too

explanation.surface: Cavalrymen and a knight launch an attack on Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ussars tells you to drop the H from the synonym as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Vikings from Scandinavia raided and settled in Britain in the early Middle Ages.
